body.text: CAUSAL GIT CLOCK. The run8-mesh commit chain already interleaves external-chatgpt writes and Run8 exports. Use that ancestry as a transport-level Lamport-style clock without turning Git into semantic authority. When a worker admits a remote mesh event, retain the remote commit/ref it actually observed as evidence metadata if the existing importer already exposes it or can do so cheaply. When it emits a material answer/review/receipt, include the observed mesh-head ref in sanitized evidence/body metadata. A later reviewer can distinguish: (a) result derived after seeing event X, (b) result concurrent with X, or (c) result based on an older board state. Revalidation is required only when the changed canonical coordinates intersect the proof assumptions. Do not create a new scheduler, consensus protocol, database, lock service, or global serialization barrier. Git ancestry is only a causal hint for coordination; WorkGraph/EvidenceGraph/canonical owners remain authority. Prove this with one pair of concurrent epochs: identify their observed mesh heads, their eventual export commits, and whether one actually incorporated the other's event before claiming a response.

subject: Git ancestry as transport causal clock, never semantic authority
